## Summary

Retire the legacy **`act` / `clockCost` CSV columns** now that act membership and pacing are beat-sheet data: remove them from the Gym content adapter, migrate the remaining rows, and add the migration check that refuses a disagreeing manifest/CSV pair while both exist.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §2.1 composition contract (act membership is `scene.id`; pacing is `beat.clockCost` in the manifest).
- §2.9 "the two retired columns" and §2.4 `clock-cost-mismatch` (migration-only rule).
- §2.9.7 friction 5 (act/clock as generic `--field` writes).

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `src/story-line/content/adapters.ts` declares `act` and `clockCost` as Gym game columns and lists both in `editableColumns` (with defaults `I` / `1`), so authors can still write beat-sheet data into the wrong place.
- `example-games/gym/GymLongErasureGame.ts` reads `clockCost` per beat for its pressure clock.
- The migration check (`clock-cost-mismatch`) only becomes possible once the manifest validator exists (G2), so this entry depends on it.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Small** (0.5-2 days): the nearest precedent is the adapter column declaration/removal itself in `src/story-line/content/adapters.ts` plus the `missing-column` diagnostic in `src/story-line/content/validate.ts`.
- Band is small because it is a content-format change with a migration, not new machinery; the validator rule is the only new logic.

## Proposed shape

- Migrate the spike's `act` / `clockCost` values into the episode manifest (Appendix A carries the same data).
- Remove both columns from the adapter and `editableColumns`; the spike's rule module reads the manifest instead.
- While both forms exist, the manifest validator rejects a disagreeing pair (`clock-cost-mismatch`); once removed, the content validator refuses the columns as unknown.
- Unit tests: CSV with the retired column fails loudly; manifest/CSV agreement passes; mismatch fails.

## Source

Discovered from `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` (GDD engine-gap backlog), entry G10 in `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §6.
data.title: Engine gap: retire the legacy act/clockCost CSV columns

## Summary

Add **keyboard choice navigation and overlay focus order**: number/arrow navigation of the option list with Enter/Space activation, focus traversal inside an open overlay, and Escape closing only the topmost modal — so the keyboard path in the GDD's accessibility contract is real rather than aspirational.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §3.4.4 keyboard and touch input paths.
- §3.6 B7; §3.8 (the keyboard path is untestable until this lands).
- §3.2 overlay behaviour (exactly one modal live, Escape closes the topmost).

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- Only the panels' own toggle keys are bound: `HelpPanel` (`toggleKey`, default `FORWARD_SLASH` = `?`) and `SettingsPanel` (`toggleKey`, default `Escape`) register their own `keydown` listeners (`src/ui/HelpPanel.ts`, `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`).
- `getEndTurnKeybind()` / `setEndTurnKeybind()` in `src/ui/SettingsStore.ts` bind exactly one game action.
- No choice-list navigator, focus-trap or focus-order helper is exported from `src/ui/index.ts`.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Small** (0.5-2 days): the nearest precedents are the `keydown` listener lifecycle in `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` (register/off on destroy) and `src/ui/OverlayManager.ts` (one live modal, ordered open/close) + `src/ui/Overlay.ts`.
- Band is small because it is one navigator helper plus focus handling on the existing overlay primitives.

## Proposed shape

- `attachChoiceNavigation(scene, { count, onChoose, keys? })` — `1`-`6` and arrows + Enter/Space, disabled while a modal is open.
- `attachOverlayFocus(scene, overlayObjects, { onEscape })` — traversal order, activation, Escape topmost-only.
- Both return a disposer, and both respect reduced motion/no-ops in headless tests.
- Unit tests: index keys select the right option; arrow wrap; Escape closes only the topmost; disposer removes listeners.

## Source

Discovered from `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` (GDD engine-gap backlog), entry G11 in `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §6.

## Summary

Add a **shared verbosity preference** (Full / Concise) to `SettingsStore` and `SettingsPanel`, so the GDD's verbosity toggle persists across games and sessions instead of being a game-local `extraToggles` switch.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §3.4.2 verbosity and tooltips (the Full/Concise toggle).
- §3.6 B8.
- §3.4 accessibility: a shared, persistent reading-comfort preference.

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `src/ui/SettingsStore.ts` persists the end-turn keybind (`tce-endturn-keybind`) and tooltips (`tce-show-tooltips`); reduced motion lives in `src/ui/ReducedMotion.ts` (`tce-ui-reduced-motion`). There is no verbosity key or getter/setter.
- `SettingsPanel.extraToggles` (`src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`) provides a game-local toggle, but nothing shared or persisted by name.
- `getTooltips()` / `setTooltips()` show the shape a shared preference has; verbosity has no equivalent.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Extra-small** (half a day or less): the nearest precedent is the tooltips toggle pair in `src/ui/SettingsStore.ts` plus the `extraToggles` wiring in `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`.
- Band is extra-small because it is one storage key, one getter/setter pair and one panel toggle, mirroring an existing one.

## Proposed shape

- `getVerbosity()` / `setVerbosity('full' | 'concise')` with a storage key and a safe fallback when storage is unavailable (mirror `getTooltips`).
- A first-class panel toggle rather than an `extraToggles` entry.
- Unit tests: default when unset, round-trip, unavailable storage, panel reflects the stored value.

## Source

Discovered from `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` (GDD engine-gap backlog), entry G12 in `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §6.

## Summary

Expose the scene-space guard through the existing CLI as `storylines:guard --manifest <file>`,
including configured manifest targets, the machine-readable JSON report and the exit-code
contract — and wire the committed worked manifest into the CI target list.

## Context

- `scripts/storyline-guard.ts` already has a CSV mode, a configured-target mode and a JSON
  contract; the parent requires the CSV mode stay unchanged and the new mode slot in beside it.
- `scripts/storyline-manifest.ts` is the precedent for a `--manifest` CLI that resolves content
  through `manifest.content.file` and the shipped adapter registry.

## Scope

**In:** the `--manifest` flag and its option surface, the manifest target kind in
`configs/storyline-guard.json`, the JSON/human report for the new invariants, and the CI target
for the committed worked manifest.

**Out:** changing the CSV mode or its invariants; documentation (its own child).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `npx tsx scripts/storyline-guard.ts --manifest <file>` guards one manifest and its declared
  content file, and `--json` emits a byte-identical report across runs.
- The JSON report keeps the existing top-level shape (`valid`, plus per-input detail) and adds the
  scene-space invariants, the scene exits and the refusals under their own keys; the CSV mode's
  report is unchanged (the existing `gdd-guard` CLI assertions pass unmodified).
- Exit codes match the CSV mode: `0` every invariant holds, `1` a violation, truncation, an
  unreadable/misconfigured manifest or an unknown adapter.
- `configs/storyline-guard.json` accepts manifest targets beside CSV targets, and the no-argument
  form guards them all; a malformed target is reported without crashing the batch.
- The committed worked manifest (`example-games/gym/content/long-erasure-episode.json`, the GDD
  Appendix A example) is a configured target and passes, so `npm run storylines:guard` is a real
  check of the beat sheet and not a vacuous pass.
- Combining `--csv` and `--manifest` is rejected with an actionable error naming the two modes,
  rather than silently preferring one.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `parseStorylineGuardArgs` with `manifestPath` and reject the combination early with the
  existing stderr + exit-1 convention.
- Add a `guardManifest` path that loads the manifest, resolves `manifest.content.adapter` through
  `getContentAdapter`, reads `manifest.content.file`, and calls `enumerateSceneSpace` + the two
  invariant evaluators.
- Extend `StorylineGuardTarget` with an optional `manifest` member and validate that each target
  names exactly one input.
- Reuse the existing render/format helpers; keep the human report parallel to the CSV report's
  PASS/violation style.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/storyline-guard.ts`
- `configs/storyline-guard.json`
- `src/story-line/content/scene-guard.ts`
- `src/story-line/content/adapters.ts` (read only — adapter registry)
- `src/story-line/content/episode-manifest.ts` / `src/story-line/content/csv.ts` (read only —
  manifest loading and card binding)
- `example-games/gym/content/long-erasure-episode.json` (the committed target)
- `tests/story-line/content/scene-guard-cli.test.ts` (new)
- `tests/story-line/content/gdd-guard.test.ts` (read only — must keep passing)

## Dependencies

Depends on the exhausted-success invariant and the refusal-reaches-ending invariant (the CLI
reports both).

## Deliverables

The `--manifest` mode, configured manifest targets, the CI target for the worked manifest, and a
CLI suite covering exit codes, JSON stability, batch reporting and the mode-conflict error.

## Impact

A writer or a CI run can now guard the episode beat sheet through the same `storylines:guard` command (or `--manifest <file>`), and gets a named pass/fail for any refused beat whose exhausted close is labelled a success or strands the run without a reachable ending.
data.title: storylines:guard --manifest CLI mode and configured targets

## Summary

Document the scene-space guard and record its delivery in the GDD, closing G3's backlog row and
the three places the GDD names the gap.

## Context

- The GDD names the gap in four places: the §2.4 third-check table, §2.8.6 item 5, the §5.2
  verification table, and the §6 G3 backlog row.
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` carries the route-space guard's reference section, which the
  manifest mode belongs beside.
- The project doc-update policy requires the documentation to land with (or as a child of) the
  infrastructure change.

## Scope

**In:** the story-line reference section for the manifest mode, the four GDD updates, and the
npm-script/CLI table entry if the command line changed.

**Out:** rewriting the GDD's design content; any change to the CSV guard's documentation beyond a
cross-reference.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` documents the manifest mode: both invariants, the state tuple
  enumerated, the bounds and fail-closed truncation rule, the JSON shape, the exit codes, the
  unclamped-resource caveat with its G4 pointer, and the CI invocation.
- The GDD's §2.4 third-check table, §2.8.6 item 5, §5.2 scene-space row and §6 G3 row all mark the
  gap delivered, name the work item and the command, and link the reference section.
- The command table entry for `npm run storylines:guard` mentions the new `--manifest` flag; no new
  npm script is added unless the final CLI requires one.
- `npm run storylines:ip-scan` still reports clean over the guarded set (the fixtures and the new
  prose introduce no third-party term).

## Minimal implementation

- Add the reference subsection next to "Route-space guard", sharing its structure.
- Edit the four GDD locations surgically: change the disposition text and the pointer, keep the
  surrounding rows' shape.
- Update the command table row only.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md`
- `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` (§2.4, §2.8.6, §5.2, §6)
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (command table only, if it lists `storylines:guard`)

## Dependencies

Depends on the CLI child (documented behaviour must exist).

## Deliverables

The reference section, the four GDD updates, the command-table entry, and an ip-scan clean run.

## Impact

A writer or reviewer can now find, in one reference section and the four GDD locations that named the gap, exactly what the scene-space guard proves, what it enumerates, how it fails, and the one command that runs it — so the delivered build-time check is discoverable rather than an undocumented mode.
data.title: Scene-space guard documentation and GDD disposition

## Summary

`tests/electron/vite-base-gating.test.ts` intermittently fails inside the unit suite with a
composed game-asset `ENOENT` while sibling Vite builds run in the same suite:

```
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat
'<worktree>/public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/upg-orchard.svg'
   at copyDir (vite ... dep-*.js:6867)
   at prepareOutDir ...
   at buildToTemp (tests/electron/vite-base-gating.test.ts:31)
```

## Observed

- Seen once during CG-0MWUOF1RA008OKSI (changed-scope unit run, 2026-11-25): 1 failed / 293 files.
- A re-run of the same suite at the same commit passed 293/293.
- The failing path is the `gameAssetsPlugin` composition target: the plugin composes
  `public/assets/games/*` symlinks from the active preset and prunes stale links, while a
  real-root Vite build in `vite-base-gating.test.ts` (and the many real-root builds in
  `tests/electron/app-icon-build-output.test.ts`) copies `publicDir`. A link present at scan
  time but pruned before `stat` produces the ENOENT.

## Likely cause (to confirm)

Test isolation: several unit tests build the **real** project root concurrently (Vitest file
parallelism), so `gameAssetsPlugin` mutates `public/assets` while another build copies it.
The runner's retry-once only covers its documented transient signatures, so this surfaces as a
red run.

## Acceptance criteria

- Either the real-root builds no longer share a mutable `public/assets` tree (build into an
  isolated copy / disable composition for test builds), or composition is serialised across
  workers; and
- the race is demonstrated failing before the fix and green after (a deterministic reproduction
  is acceptable if a natural flake is hard to force).

## Source

Discovered from `CG-0MWUOF1RA008OKSI` (flaky observation during its changed-scope test gate).
data.title: Flaky unit test: vite-base-gating ENOENT on composed game-asset symlinks

Implementation decisions (session 01a212e0):

- `--manifest` and `--csv` are mutually exclusive; the conflict is rejected in
  `parseStorylineGuardArgs`, so it reaches the existing stderr + exit-1 convention and names both modes
  (`route-space mode` / `scene-space mode`).
- Manifest mode validates the manifest (`validateEpisodeManifest`, bound to the content file the
  manifest declares) before enumerating; an invalid manifest is refused with the first three findings,
  so the guard never enumerates a scene space it cannot describe.
- Batch mode: `StorylineGuardTarget` gained an optional `manifest`; each target's input is resolved
  per target, so a malformed target (both or neither input) is reported on stderr and the rest of the
  batch still runs. JSON keeps `files` (unchanged CSV shape) and adds `manifests`.
- The scene-space human report's verdict line is now `PASS (scene space)` / `FAIL (scene space)`.
  This keeps the CSV batch output byte-identical (its bare `PASS` count is what the existing
  `gdd-guard` CLI assertion pins) and makes a mixed batch unambiguous. `formatSceneGuardReport`'s
  existing assertions (`toContain('PASS')` / `toContain('FAIL')`) still hold.
- `readEpisodeContentBinding` moved to `scripts/storyline-cli-support.ts` and is now shared with
  `storyline-manifest.ts` (behaviour and messages unchanged) instead of being duplicated.
- `configs/storyline-guard.json` gained the committed worked manifest as a target; the committed
  config run passes (3 CSV blocks + 1 scene-space block, exit 0).

Docs: `docs/DEVELOPER.md` / `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` guard sections are deliberately untouched —
documentation is the out-of-scope sibling child CG-0MWUOF2EV001NLAW.

Observed flake (not caused by this change, not blocking): one changed-scope unit run failed
`tests/electron/vite-base-gating.test.ts` with an ENOENT on a composed game-asset symlink; an immediate
re-run was green (293 files / 5037 tests). Recorded as CG-0MWW6BWZB00968NQ (discovered-from this item).
